principle: Using Super Técnico must be cheaper or materially more reliable than reconstructing the answer independently.

tools.name: Knowledge Compact API
tools.next_step: Implement projections that return only the minimum records and fields required for the stated objective.
tools.rationale: Highest direct reduction of tokens, document reads and repeated retrieval.

tools.name: Error Code Resolver
tools.next_step: Build a compact server projection that preserves brand, family, unit and display location.
tools.rationale: The expensive data work already exists and remote projection offers immediate reuse.

tools.name: Manual to Procedure
tools.next_step: Normalize procedures with exact model scope, source locator, safety warnings and review status.
tools.rationale: Valuable, but a procedure with the wrong model scope is riskier than a missing result.

tools.name: Component and board identifier
tools.next_step: Expose candidate identification without hiding ambiguity or historical status.
tools.rationale: Existing normalized identifiers make this cheaper than a new image or document pipeline.

tools.name: Technical component comparison
tools.next_step: Return critical differences, missing evidence and application-specific incompatibilities.
tools.rationale: High reuse and low marginal compute once the records are normalized.

tools.name: Datasheet to structured record
tools.next_step: Pilot only on high-reuse documents with permitted storage and a human verification queue.
tools.rationale: It is economical only when the same verified extraction is reused many times.

tools.name: Case Matcher
tools.next_step: Add structured symptoms, equipment scope, measurements and confirmed repair outcome.
tools.rationale: Strong differentiation, but usefulness depends on moderation and confirmed outcomes.

tools.name: Next Best Measurement
tools.next_step: Validate the refrigeration implementation before extending it to electrical and combustion diagnostics.
tools.rationale: Reduces technician and AI iterations, but every domain needs its own evidence rules.

tools.name: Technical diagnostic engine
tools.next_step: Compose reviewed rules and validators; never infer refrigerant charge or safety conclusions from one measurement.
tools.rationale: High value, but it must be assembled from validated tools instead of one opaque model call.

tools.name: Technical Answer Validator
tools.next_step: Validate decomposed claims against source IDs and deterministic rules, returning unsupported claims explicitly.
tools.rationale: Valuable to AI clients, but it cannot be trustworthy before reviewed rule coverage exists.

tools.name: Measurement Validator
tools.next_step: Implement unit, range, physical-consistency and cross-measurement checks by domain.
tools.rationale: Excellent cost-to-value ratio and a prerequisite for safe diagnostics.

tools.name: Technical case normalizer
tools.next_step: Create separate schemas for refrigeration, electrical, combustion and field-service cases.
tools.rationale: A universal normalizer built too early would erase important domain distinctions.

tools.name: Deterministic Calculators API
tools.next_step: Extract versioned pure functions and expose focused endpoints rather than one generic calculator.
tools.rationale: Best immediate economics: tiny inputs and outputs, deterministic execution and high reuse.

tools.name: Technical simulators
tools.next_step: Reconsider only after demand, validation datasets and deterministic calculators are mature.
tools.rationale: High infrastructure and validation cost before the simpler tools prove commercial demand.

tools.name: AI Quality Auditor
tools.next_step: Define a scored rubric only after blind benchmark cases and adjudicated answers exist.
tools.rationale: An auditor without a trusted gold set would merely add another unverified opinion.

tools.name: HVAC/R AI Benchmark
tools.next_step: Run the internal economic benchmark during phase zero; expose a B2B benchmark only after independent review.
tools.rationale: The internal benchmark is mandatory now, while the commercial benchmark is a later product.
